2. **Read the viewer.** `gh api user --jq .login` returns `alex`. That becomes `viewer.login`.

3. **Run the author query.**
   `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json number,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions`
   It exits 0 with 6 rows, which is below the 1000 limit. Every row is an object with an integer `number`.

4. **Run the direct-request query.**
   `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'user-review-requested:@me' --state open --limit 1000 --json number,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions`
   It exits 0 with 4 rows, which is below the limit. Every row is well-formed.

5. **Union, dedupe and filter.**
   - #101 appears in both queries, so it is kept once.
   - #200 is a draft, so it is excluded.
   - #201 is `APPROVED`, so it is excluded.
   - #202 is `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, so it is excluded.
   - #112 has a `null` decision and #97 has `""`. Neither is exactly `APPROVED` or `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, so both stay.

6. **Sort by additions+deletions, then by number.**

   | PR | Size |
   |---|---|
   | #101 | 2 |
   | #97 | 4 |
   | #112 | 6 |
   | #88 | 8 |
   | #130 | 8 |
   | #104 | 10 |

   #88 and #130 tie at 8, so #88 sorts first by number.

7. **Route the six matches.** Six matches on pi re-enter set routing with origin URL tokens and `source: discovered`:
   - `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/101`
   - `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/97`
   - `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/112`
   - `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/88`
   - `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/130`
   - `https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/104`

8. **Run set-routing admission.** This happens before any fetch, confirmation, provisioning or dispatch.
   - There are no positional issue refs.
   - There are no duplicate identities.
   - All tokens match origin.
   - The harness is pi.
   - pi-cohort `parallel.maxTasks` is 4 and the set has 6, so the set is oversized. It is rejected, never chunked or trimmed.
